FROMGIT: media: mtk-vcodec: fix access to vb2_v4l2_buffer struct Commit 0650a91499e0 ("media: mtk-vcodec: Correct return type for mem2mem buffer helpers") fixed the return types for mem2mem buffer helper functions, but omitted two occurrences that are accessed in the mtk_v4l2_debug() macro. These only trigger compiler errors when DEBUG is defined. Fixes: 0650a91499e0 ("media: mtk-vcodec: Correct return type for mem2mem buffer helpers") BUG=b:123551776 TEST=Build Kukui image. Signed-off-by: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl> Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 3235d3946429f64b19addfd89fc926a36eaec06a git://linuxtv.org/media_tree.git) Change-Id: Ibed39067caf85c3d97c68b06420997a370cc8a74 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1545385 Commit-Ready: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Tested-by: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: media: mtk-vcodec: fix access to incorrect planes member Commit 0650a91499e0 ("media: mtk-vcodec: Correct return type for mem2mem buffer helpers") fixed the return types for mem2mem buffer helper functions by changing a few local variables from vb2_buffer to vb2_v4l2_buffer. However, it left a few accesses to vb2_buffer::planes as-is, accidentally turning them into accesses to vb2_v4l2_buffer::planes and resulting in values being read from/written to the wrong place. Fix this by inserting vb2_buf into these accesses so they mimic their original behavior. Fixes: 0650a91499e0 ("media: mtk-vcodec: Correct return type for mem2mem buffer helpers") BUG=b:123551776 TEST=Build Kukui image. Signed-off-by: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ezequiel Garcia <ezequiel@collabora.com> Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl> Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 52fafc58c3535c9f4f53864686dbaee3bcbadcb4 git://linuxtv.org/media_tree.git) Change-Id: I4595d10ec14ece41f0ad1246b19ac3f866c7ed51 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1545386 Commit-Ready: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Tested-by: Alexandre Courbot <acourbot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org>

drivers/storage/nvme: Update NVME CQS size for Intel Optane memory There was an issue with Intel optane NVME devices where Phase bit is not correctly updated for polled command completions when QD>12. This results in timeout while reading from NVME devices. Reducing NVME_CSQ_SIZE and NVME_CCQ_SIZE to 11 will fix this issue. Change-Id: I4cb70bed1f42d49f9bedcc28b8382cb1da16cf78 Signed-off-by: Maulik V Vaghela <maulik.v.vaghela@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1535090 Commit-Ready: Maulik V Vaghela <maulik.v.vaghela@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Tested-by: Maulik V Vaghela <maulik.v.vaghela@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: HID: intel-ish-hid: ISH firmware loader client driver This driver adds support for loading Intel Integrated Sensor Hub (ISH) firmware from host file system to ISH SRAM and start execution. At power-on, the ISH subsystem shall boot to an interim Shim loader-firmware, which shall expose an ISHTP loader device. The driver implements an ISHTP client that communicates with the Shim ISHTP loader device over the intel-ish-hid stack, to download the main ISH firmware. (am from https://lkml.org/lkml/2019/4/2/63) BUG=b:122722008 TEST=Build kernel, boot & verify that Intel ISH FW is successfully loaded by the driver (requires ISH FW to be present under /lib/firmware/intel) Signed-off-by: Rushikesh S Kadam <rushikesh.s.kadam@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Rushikesh S Kadam <rushikesh.s.kadam@intel.corp-partner.google.com> Acked-by: Srinivas Pandruvada <srinivas.pandruvada@linux.intel.com> Acked-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Tested-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Change-Id: Id80211ace8e15ab21d18b04b8cf74845e8d426f5 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1433481

CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Enable BLuetooth LE splitter for x86-64 With this change, BT splitter can be used and newblue can be run. By default the functionality of the splitter is disabled (CL:1352383) and users can enable it by using the crosh command (CL:1121542). For now x86-64 is prioritized and this will be enabled on all other architectures as well later on. BUG=chromium:859239,chromium:909045 TEST=With this built on nami, enable and disable newblue and check that splitter is indeed enabled and disabled. Check that by default (splitter disabled) Bluetooth works normally. Change-Id: If57c803df3937a815a6418b3592733dfd96969e2 Signed-off-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1547991 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Reviewed-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org>
